answer: Like yarrow spreading only where roots already hold soil, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a small refundable stake before it may trade. Newcomers start in a probationary grove: transactions settle slowly and reputation accrues only after counterparties confirm real delivery. If an agent cheats or floods the market with clones, its stake is slashed and the delta between promised and delivered value is published to every peer, so copies share one reputation ledger and cannot multiply trust. Standing grows from verified work, not headcount.
